title: Ultramarathon runners and support crew: The influence of pre-race sleep and training profiles on performance in a 217-km mountain race
authors: Daniel NVS, Barreira J, Bastos AM, Dos Santos NE, Franco B, Esteves AM, Belli T
population: 38 ultramarathon runners and 59 support crew members in a 217-km mountain race, assessed by questionnaire.
findings: 38 runners and 59 crew members answered questionnaires on chronotype, sleep quality, sleepiness, demographics and pre-race training.
Training frequency was highly correlated with race time (r = -0.59).
Athletes with good sleep quality trained one day more per week than those without (p < 0.001).
Finishers had higher sleep latency than non-finishers (p < 0.001).
The abstract reports no longest-run value.
limitations: Very small runner sample, questionnaire, many comparisons, no longest-run data; relevance to the question is low (training frequency only).
implications: Weakly supports training frequency over single-session size for beyond-100-mile races; no support for a 270 min longest-run number.

verification.notes: Re-fetched Crossref (Sleep Med, 2024-08, Daniel) and Europe PMC abstract (PMID 38909481). r = -0.59 and both p < 0.001 values match. Kept as marginally relevant (training frequency in a >100-mile race); no long-run data.
